# Cross-Exchange Liquidity Commentary — 31 July 2026

The US exchanges dominate the liquidity hierarchy. NYSE leads decisively with the lowest ILLIQ metric at 0.0059% per $1M traded and commanding comparable volume of $223.4M, while Nasdaq 100 follows closely with the tightest absolute spreads at 0.8432% AR spread but superior price stability at 0.0025% per $1M traded and higher turnover at 1.3470%. European and Asian tier-one markets—Euronext, Tokyo, and Hong Kong—form a solid middle tier, each posting ILLIQ readings between 0.0301% and 0.0377% per $1M traded with comparable volumes ranging from $15.2M to $49.8M. A notable divergence emerges in SIX Swiss Exchange, which offers the tightest spreads at 0.4993% AR spread yet carries minimal comparable volume of $3.1M and middling ILLIQ costs of 0.0451% per $1M traded, suggesting tight tick-level pricing masks low absolute liquidity. The secondary tier—Xetra and London—show elevated execution costs, with LSE's ILLIQ reaching 0.0798% per $1M traded and 0.8179% spreads despite modest turnover. Korea Exchange lags substantially, with ILLIQ of 0.1559% per $1M traded and the widest spreads at 1.5734% AR spread, though its 1.4018% turnover ratio hints at domestic activity concentration misaligned with international comparable liquidity.
